title: Quantum Fine-Grained Lower Bounds for SetDisjointness via Sub-Linear Reductions from 3SUM
authors: Jeremy Huang, Young Kun Ko, Chunhao Wang
abstract: In classical fine-grained complexity, the 3SUM Conjecture is used to prove a variety of conditional lower bounds on data structure and graph problems via an initial reduction to the SetDisjointness problem. However, there is an $\tilde{O}(n)$-time quantum algorithm for 3SUM and a direct application of Grover's algorithm to SetDisjointness queries beats the state-of-the-art classical conditional bound by Kopelowitz, Pettie, and Porat (SODA 2016); this shows that these classical bounds do not apply in the quantum setting. Thus establishing analogous conditional lower bounds in the quantum setting requires applying the quantum 3SUM Conjecture to a \emph{quantum} fine-grained reduction from 3SUM to SetDisjointness.   We give the first sub-linear time quantum reductions from 3SUM to online SetDisjointness. Via our reduction, the quantum 3SUM conjecture implies a $p + 2q \geqslant 1$ tradeoff bound for quantum SetDisjointness algorithms with $O(N^p)$ preprocessing time and $O(N^q)$ query time. We also give an analogous reduction from 3XOR. These results are derived from a general framework for fine-grained reductions to SetDisjointness which applies to any Abelian 3-Orthogonal Array (3OA) problem with suitable almost-linear hash functions.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to prove quantum lower bounds for the online SetDisjointness problem by reducing it from the 3SUM problem. By achieving sub-linear quantum reductions, the authors establish a new tradeoff bound ($p + 2q \ge 1$) for SetDisjointness, showing that classical complexity results do not translate directly to the quantum setting.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish quantum fine-grained conditional lower bounds for the online SetDisjointness problem by reducing it from the 3SUM problem and related Abelian 3-Orthogonal Array (3OA) problems.
main_result: They derive a quantum tradeoff bound for Online SetDisjointness: $p + 2q \geqslant 1$, conditional on the quantum 3SUM conjecture, which improves upon classical bounds.
method: The core method involves constructing sub-linear time quantum reductions from 3SUM/3OA to SetDisjointness using advanced techniques like L-subset finding quantum walks and optimized hash-bucket data structures.
model_or_system: The analysis is conducted within the standard quantum circuit model, focusing on the complexity of quantum algorithms for specific computational problems (3SUM, SetDisjointness) rather than a physical quantum system.
key_observables: The primary observables are the time complexities $p$ (preprocessing) and $q$ (query time) for solving SetDisjointness, constrained by the derived tradeoff $p + 2q \ge 1$.
important_parameters: The key parameters include the exponents $p$ and $q$, the size parameters $n$ (instance size) and $N$ (SetDisjointness instance size), and the parameter $\gamma$ used in the reduction complexity.
main_assumptions: The results are highly conditional on the quantum 3SUM conjecture and the existence of specific, efficient families of hash functions.
paper_structure: The paper builds a general framework for fine-grained reductions to SetDisjointness, first establishing the quantum 3SUM reduction, then generalizing this to 3OA problems, and finally deriving the conditional lower bound $p + 2q \ge 1$ for online SetDisjointness.
why_interesting: While the topic is computational complexity, the reliance on quantum algorithms (quantum walks, amplitude amplification) and the establishment of quantum lower bounds place it at the intersection of quantum computation theory and complexity theory, which is relevant to understanding the limits of quantum information processing.
